D.t: Amanda Janoo trails by 5.1 and wins 21% of simulations. Closing it takes about 8,395 voters switching sides, or 16,790 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +13.2 and D +3.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +1.1. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +6.3; your worst is Braun Research at R +9.3. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Chittenden, a projected net 11,861 votes; Windham, a projected net 6,349 votes; Washington, a projected net 1,911 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Washington, D +6.0, 9.6% of the vote; Windsor, R +2.0, 9.3% of the vote; Addison, R +4.2, 6.1% of the vote; Bennington, R +5.7, 5.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Amanda Janoo runs furthest behind in Grand Isle, Lamoille, Franklin. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 45 to 52, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Small counties, 73% of voters, 43 to 55, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.64 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 49 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.60 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Amanda Janoo: Immigration voters 15 to 83, 2024 nonvoters and third party voters 24 to 73, Independents 27 to 69. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$307K cash against $202K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Air cover: Outside groups spent $400K helping Phil Scott and $40K helping Amanda Janoo.

R.t: Phil Scott leads by 5.1 in the forecast and wins 79% of simulations. The cushion is about 16,790 votes; a one point swing is about 1,646 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +3.2 and R +13.2. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is R +1.1. Your best recent poll is Braun Research at R +9.3; your worst is University of New Hampshire at D +6.3. 4 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Rutland, a projected net 10,370 votes; Franklin, a projected net 9,235 votes; Orleans, a projected net 4,453 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Washington, D +6.0, 9.6% of the vote; Windsor, R +2.0, 9.3% of the vote; Addison, R +4.2, 6.1% of the vote; Bennington, R +5.7, 5.6% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Phil Scott runs furthest behind in Windham, Bennington, Orleans. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 52 to 45, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Small counties, 73% of voters, 55 to 43, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.64 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 49 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.60 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Phil Scott: Health care and Social Security voters 38 to 60, Corruption voters 39 to 59, Midsize counties 43 to 56. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$202K cash against $307K. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.

National tide: Gallup party identification moved from Republicans 48 Democrats 45 in the third quarter of 2024 to Democrats 50 Republicans 39 in the third quarter of 2026, 14 points toward the Democrats.
